summary: DeckCraft is a presentation app, like Microsoft PowerPoint or Apple Keynote. You make slides with text, pictures and charts. You can save the slides as a PowerPoint file.
use_cases: Make a short deck for a team meeting from a list of results.
Show survey results in a chart that you can edit later.
Make a new version of the same deck every month with new numbers.
Send a .pptx file to colleagues who use PowerPoint.
story: DeckCraft made a 7-slide deck about the study. The slides show the method, 3 findings, the main takeaway and a note about the invented data. VectorCraft made the 3 charts on slides 2, 3 and 4. DeckCraft drew the chart on slide 5 itself. The deck has transitions between slides and animations on the slides. It opens in PowerPoint.
recipe_note: Make a slide. Save the deck as a PowerPoint file. Export each slide as a PNG image.

assets.description: A short Python script joined the 7 slide images from DeckCraft into 1 animated GIF. The same Python script made the short fades between the GIF images, not DeckCraft.
assets.how: Python/PIL (_work/deckcraft/gif.py): slide PNGs from deckcraft-cli render --all, 5 blend frames between slides, 128 colours. DeckCraft has no video or GIF export.

headless_notes: run, render and convert worked without a window. run has no references to earlier results, but a new object stays selected, so the next format command changes it. run writes only the last --save, so convert made the .pptx file. design.colors set the study colours, so the native chart uses them. The transitions and animations stay in the .pptx file. DeckCraft cannot render them to video or GIF, so a Python script made the GIF from the slide images. The PDF is about 2 MB because it contains the slide pictures at full size.
